references.text: Jesus meets Simon (Peter) and Andrew by the Sea of Galilee and calls them to follow him – this parallels Jesus using Simon's boat here.
Jesus sits in a boat and teaches the crowd from the water, just as he does here in Luke 5:3.
Jesus asks the disciples to keep a small boat ready for him because of the crowd, showing the same pattern of using a boat to manage the throng of people.
Mark's parallel where Jesus sits in a boat on the sea and teaches the crowd standing on land – a very close parallel to Luke 5:3.
Shortly before this event, Jesus taught the crowds in Capernaum, and they were amazed at his teaching – this shows his continuous ministry of teaching.
Simon Peter's reaction after the miraculous catch of fish leads him and his partners to leave everything and follow Jesus – a continuation of this story confirming Simon's central role.
After the resurrection, Jesus meets the disciples again by the sea and is involved in a miraculous catch of fish from a boat, an event that echoes Luke 5:3-7.
Jesus sits down to teach the crowds (the Sermon on the Mount) – sitting was the usual posture for a Jewish teacher, just as he does from the boat in Luke 5:3.
